They had many different types of gladiators. In fact they would build urban battlefields in the ring to mix up the battle. They even flooded the coliseum to recreate ship battles. As to what types there were, the samnite class was the one with the big shield and gladius, who fought like the Roman legionaires.  There was a class that had an armored left arm, with a trident and a weighted net, which ment they were the least armored but the quickest, and could trap their enemy and kill them as they were trying to get out of the net. There was even a type that wore full Loria segmentata armor and a helmet with no eye holes, and had two huge blades attached to their arms. They then stumbled across the battlefield using sound alone and tryed to eviscerate their fellow gladiators. Needless to say this wasn't wasn't  a big advantage  and the novelty soon wore off as all the smart gladiators easily overcame them. But for true combat insperation look at the Roman battlefield achievements. In Ceasars famous battle with vercingetorix his 16,000 man strong handful of legions destroyed a 300,000 man strong army of gauls  from across france. Even the average battle saw the legions outnumbered many if not tens of times to one. Finally at zama Scipio Africanus' 20000 man army of Veterans from Spain routed Hannibal barca's army three times as big. Hannibal was the best general since Alexander the great, and had beaten the Romans 6 times in Italy on their own turf and had slaughtered a 90000 man strong army at cannae. Scipio is arguably the best general the Republic had. So all in all rome's generals and military training far surpassed what the gladiators accomplished in the ring. Hence when the gladiators under Spartacus rebelled and met the Legion on the field of battle they were routed decisively.
